To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

single cylindrical submicron scale pores in a PMMA membrane are micropatternable by electron beam lithographic processes, that they can be integrated into all types of PMMA-based electroporetic flow detector (EFD) systems, that their electrical characteristics can be measured, and that they can be used to detect the passage of single-stranded DNA molecules through protein channels.
PMMA membranes with micrometer scale cylindrical pores are suitable for use in all PMMA electroporetic flow detector devices.

single cylindrical submicron-scale pores in PMMA membranes are suitable for the detection of biological particles in aqueous electrolytes, and that their electrical properties are stable, linear, and reproducible.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the electrical characterization of submicron pores and their applicability in resistive-pulse biomolecule detection.
the fabrication and electrical characterization of single cylindrical submicron pore PMMA membranes.
the development of a new generation of resistive-pulse detectors that are based on PMMA membranes and that allow the detection of single biomolecules.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

PMMA membranes are an excellent choice as a base material for all electrophoretic detection devices, as well as for resistive-pulse sensing, as long as the pore dimensions match the size of the biomolecule of interest.

PMMA-based electroporation and resistive-pulse detection systems are excellent tools to investigate and characterize the electrical properties of biological pores in aqueous solutions, as well as their application for biomolecule detection.
our PMMA-based electroporetic flow detector is an excellent candidate for the development of a new generation of resistive-pulse biomolecule sensors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have successfully developed a new class of polymer-based nanopores that exhibit the same properties as those of nanopores in silicon nitride membranes, but with the advantage of being much more easily fabricated and integrated into electrophoretic systems.
the described PMMA electrophoresis-based flow detector systems are well-suited for the detection of biomolecules, as long as they can be transported through pores of the same dimensions.
PMMA membranes with submicron pores, which are micropatternable and integratable into PMMA-based electroporetic flow detectors, are promising candidates as resistive-pulse sensor membranes.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the presented PMMA-based electropores can be used as an alternative to the currently most widely used nanopores in silicon nitride membranes, as long as the pore dimensions are in the submicron range.
the PMMA-based system is a viable platform to develop resistive-pulse biomolecule sensors, as long the dimensions of the pores are in the same order of magnitude as the biomolecules to be analyzed.

PMMA polymer membranes, which have been used in all PMMA electropores-based electrophoretically driven flow detector systems, are not only suitable for the fabrication of micropatterned single cylindrical submicron scale pores, but also allow for the integration of protein pores into the membrane, thus enabling the detection of biomolecules by resistive pulses.
